newsitem.title: MEXICO: RESEARCH ALERT - Camesa started as strong buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Camesa started as strong buy.

text.p: Mexican steel wire and cable and fluorspar producer Grupo Industrial Camesa was started Wednesday as a "strong buy" recommendation by Interacciones brokerage.
Interacciones analyst Sebastian Barry-Taylor said from both a comparative P/E and P/CF analysis Camesa appears attractive.

"A DCF analysis reinforces this view as do EV/EBIDTA multiples of 3.4 times for 1997 and 2.4 times for 1998. Our estimated price target range for year-end 1997 is 6.14-6.30 pesos, giving an annualized dollar return of approximately 31 percent," Barry-Taylor said in a report. "We initiate coverage with a strong buy recommendation," he added.
Camesa experienced an impressive turnaround in fortunes in 1995, with sales growing 88 percent against 1994 and operating margins jumping to 26 percent from one percent, Barry-Taylor said.

"Although devaluation played a significant part in boosting revenues and margins, management began to implement an aggressive restructuring and expansion program which we believe has placed the company in a position to register strong sustainable growth for the foreseeable future," he said.

Barry-Taylor added that aggressive expansion of production capacity in both divisions and the establishment of foreign distribution channels form the cornerstone of management strategy. Due to accords with distributors in Britain and Japan in particular, Camesa is hitting new markets, he said.

Also, Camesa is changing its product mix to be more value- added. Camesa's mining division will start producing low arsenic content acidspar by the fourth quarter of 1997, which carries a price premium over other fluorspar products. "We estimate that operating profit will grow by 29.0 percent in 1996, 19.0 percent 1997 and 16.6 percent in 1998," he said.

Camesa's financial position is now solid after being rescued from virtual bankruptcy in 1993. "Debt with cost/equity is 32 percent and interest coverage is 13 times. We estimate EBITDA will grow 21 percent in 1996 and 17.5 percent in 1997," the analyst added.
